project.name: code2req
project.vision: Spec-Driven Development (SDD) — treating a highly structured, technology-agnostic business specification as the primary, authoritative artifact from which automated tests, clean implementation, and functional documentation are derived.
project.elevator_pitch: An AI-driven CLI that reverse-engineers legacy enterprise codebases into structured business specifications organized by functional flows, with full traceability back to source code.
project.problem_statement: Legacy enterprise codebases contain embedded business rules, domain validations, and ecosystem invariants that are obscured by technical debt and scattered across REST endpoints, async event handlers, and hidden procedural database layers — making systems hard to understand, test, and re-architect.
goals: De-technify enterprise code — abstract dense, legacy implementations into clear business intentions, process parameters, and edge cases
Eradicate context rot & hallucinations — enforce stateless, short-lived execution with absolute context isolation per file
Provide end-to-end visibility — connect scattered functional points across frontend, REST, async events, and database layers
Provide a standard data contract for test generation — output predictable structured semantic graphs bridging static code and dynamic business tests

stakeholders.name: Developer
concerns: Quickly understand legacy codebases without manual reading
Extract business rules obscured by technical debt
Generate structured specifications from source code

stakeholders.name: Tech Lead
concerns: No leakage of secrets or credentials

user_personas.name: Developer
goals: Understand what business rules a legacy codebase implements

pain_points: Spending hours reading through dense legacy code

Lack of documentation on system behavior and edge cases
user_personas.context: Works with Java/Spring codebases daily. Needs to quickly onboard to unfamiliar legacy systems or document existing ones for compliance and refactoring.

user_personas.name: Tech Lead
goals: Ensure sensitive data never leaves local machine
pain_points: No reliable way to get a bird's-eye view of a legacy system
Risk of hardcoded secrets leaking through AI pipelines
Difficulty tracing async event flows across services
user_personas.context: Responsible for architectural decisions and compliance. Needs to trust the tool's output and verify nothing sensitive is exposed.

technical: Pure Java — no native OS bindings or JNI (no Tree-sitter)

compliance: Read-only operation — zero modifications to source files

Processing tasks that reach SUCCESS state (excluding AWAITING_HUMAN_REVIEW)
Zero exceptions due to file locks when executing under pool-size of 10 with WAL mode

success_metrics.target: 0 tokens consumed on re-scan of unchanged workspace
success_metrics.measurement: Re-running against unmodified workspace completes using 100% cached records in <= 60 seconds
Time to resolve pending/orphaned states and re-align the processing DAG after crash
Ratio of resolved MethodCallExpr nodes to total non-JDK MethodCallExpr nodes in the codebase
Verification that all @Procedure annotations and JdbcTemplate calls are captured
Verification that all RestTemplate/WebClient/FeignClient usages are registered as floating_links
Cross-reference of matching topic/queue/destination pairs between producers and consumers
Only files exceeding llm-unresolved-threshold or flagged by semantic criteria qualify for LLM enrichment
Ratio of fully-extracted functional flows to total candidate flows inferred by the Embabel agent

non_functional_requirements.description: Hardcoded secrets must be redacted in-memory before any LLM processing

risks.description: JavaParser fails on complex or vendor-specific syntax constructs
risks.mitigation: Annotation-driven fallback strategy — classify components by annotation presence even when type resolution fails

risks.description: SQLite locking under concurrent access during Phase 2 (design concern carried forward)
risks.mitigation: WAL mode + busy_timeout + connection pool configured upfront in Phase 1 implementation

risks.description: Process crash during Phase 1 leaves SQLite task store in inconsistent state with orphaned RUNNING tasks
risks.mitigation: Startup orphan detection and reconciliation; resume command for explicit warm-start recovery

risks.description: Secret redaction misses non-standard credential patterns or produces false positives on benign values
risks.mitigation: Pattern-based detection with documented coverage scope; in-memory only operation limits blast radius

risks.description: JavaParser version incompatibility with Java language features used in target codebase (e.g., records, sealed classes, pattern matching)
risks.mitigation: Pin compatible JavaParser version; graceful parse failure per file with logged error does not block full scan

epics.name: Deterministic Multi-Language Indexing
epics.description: Before any LLM interaction, the CLI scans the physical workspace using pure-Java AST parsers (JavaParser) to map signatures, endpoint routes, call frameworks, and event publishers. Produces a local intermediate JSON contract and populates the SQLite task store. Runs as a deterministic compiler-pass requiring zero network connectivity or LLM credentials.

epics.name: Language Extension Framework (Postponed)
epics.description: Define a common parser abstraction (SPI) so that adding support for new programming languages does not require modifying the core pipeline. Language parsers implement a shared contract and are discovered at runtime. The rest of the pipeline (redaction, output, orchestration) remains parser-agnostic. E002 is formally postponed — retained for future reference.

epics.name: Semantic Enrichment (Embedded in extract)
epics.description: Per ADR-006, enrichment is not a standalone Phase 2 — it runs as a GOAP action (EnrichFlowAction) inside the extract command. LlmEnrichmentService handles LLM calls with StructuralContextAssembler providing Phase 1 context. No separate plan/enrich CLI commands exist.

epics.name: Agentic Functional Requirement Extraction (Embabel GOAP)
epics.description: Phase 3 of the pipeline: an Embabel GOAP agent discovers entry points, traces execution flows through the call graph, and extracts functional requirements (user stories, Gherkin scenarios, business rules). Persists intermediate results to extraction-cache.json; a separate generate command produces the Markdown specification and semantic_manifest.json from the cache.

epics.name: Snapshot & Restore
epics.description: Point-in-time snapshots of local state (SQLite database + JSON index) for safe experimentation and rollback during iterative analysis. VACUUM INTO creates transactionally consistent copies without stopping the application.

features.name: Two-Pass Pipeline Orchestration & Call Graph Resolution
features.description: Two-pass deterministic linker: Pass 1 collects method signatures into a GlobalDeclarationRegistry; Pass 2 resolves MethodCallExpr nodes against the registry to produce CallGraphEdge records. Overloaded methods recorded as AMBIGUOUS when arguments cannot discriminate.
features.background: Phase 4a (ComponentVisitor, EndpointVisitor) completed. Pipeline refactored to two-pass orchestration.
business_rules: Pass 1 extracts method signatures, field types, and component stereotypes — no resolution or analysis is performed
Pass 2 resolves each MethodCallExpr against the declaration registry built in Pass 1
Calls matching internal package boundaries are recorded with source file, target file, and method signatures
Overloaded methods are recorded as AMBIGUOUS when argument count cannot discriminate
Calls to JDK, Spring internals, and unresolvable third-party libraries are recorded as unresolved_signatures
Post-pass runs TopicLinkResolver and FloatingLinkResolver after all files are processed
Parse errors in one file do not block processing of other files

Detect @Procedure(name) on repository methods

Spring Data interfaces (CrudRepository, JpaRepository) registered as virtual database access points

features.name: Outbound HTTP Detection & Floating Link Resolution

features.name: Flow-Driven Enrichment Qualification
features.description: EnrichFlowAction.shouldEnrich() evaluates whether files in a traced flow need LLM enrichment using inline qualification checks: stored procedures, custom validators, complex SQL, unresolved HTTP calls, test file pairing, AOP advice links, and complex entry points. No standalone Planner or rule-engine plugin architecture was built.
features.background: Phase 1 indexing completed with tasks and findings in SQLite.
business_rules: A file qualifies if it contains a DATABASE_PROCEDURE_CALL, CONSTRAINT_VALIDATOR, NATIVE_SQL_QUERY, or JPQL_HQL_QUERY finding
A file qualifies if it has unresolved floating links (PENDING status)
A file qualifies if it has a paired test file or AOP advice links
A file qualifies if it is an entry point with ComplexityLevel >= STANDARD
Qualification runs inside extract, not as a standalone step

user_stories.title: Planner qualifies tasks for LLM enrichment

features.name: LLM Executor Framework — Per-file Semantic Enrichment
features.description: Individual file enrichment workers (LlmEnrichmentService). Each executor receives structural context from Phase 1 (via StructuralContextAssembler) plus raw source file content, calls Spring AI ChatClient, validates output against JSON Schema, and persists ExecutionFinding to SQLite. Called from within EnrichFlowAction during extract.
features.background: EnrichFlowAction has determined files need enrichment. @Async pool configured.
business_rules: Executor receives structural context (call graph edges, endpoints, database access, link registrations)
LLM prompt instructs model NOT to resolve structural dependencies — focus on business semantics only
Output must validate against JSON Schema before task transitions to ENRICHED
Invalid output transitions task to ENRICH_FAILED with structural error classification
On HTTP 429, exponential backoff: 2s initial, 2.0 multiplier, 60s cap, 3 max retries
Context budget: if combined tokens exceed 80% of model window, pre-summarize companion logic

user_stories.title: Executor enriches a single file with LLM

features.name: Embedded Enrichment in Extract
features.description: EnrichFlowAction manages enrichment concurrency within the extract command using a dedicated thread pool. It fires CompletableFuture for each qualifying file, joins results before AnalyzeFlow runs, and uses a ConcurrentHashMap cache to avoid duplicating enrichment across flows. No standalone Orchestrator or dynamic re-planning was built.
features.background: EnrichFlowAction invoked during extract. Thread pool configured.
business_rules: Files are enriched concurrently via CompletableFuture on a dedicated thread pool
CompletableFuture.allOf().join() blocks until all files in the flow are enriched
Enrichment cache (ConcurrentHashMap) avoids enriching the same file across multiple flows
No dynamic re-planning — discovered_dependencies are parsed and logged but not re-batched

features.name: CLI Commands — run
features.description: The run command orchestrates scan → extract → generate end-to-end. Status command provides task counts and flow extraction metrics. No standalone plan/enrich commands exist — enrichment is embedded in extract via EnrichFlowAction.
features.background: All pipeline components implemented.
business_rules: run --manifest path orchestrates scan → extract → generate
run --dry-run uses deterministic stubs with zero API spend
status shows task counts by status and flow extraction metrics

features.description: Uncomment and configure the Embabel dependency in pom.xml. Embabel provides the GOAP (Goal-Oriented Action Planning) engine for Phase 3's agentic functional requirement extraction.

features.name: CodebaseKnowledge Builder + Phase 3 Orchestrator
features.description: Pure-Java services that aggregate Phase 1 findings and enrichment data into CodebaseKnowledge with query methods for entry points, call graph traversal, component discovery, and orphaned method detection. ExtractionOrchestrator builds the model, passes it to the Embabel agent, and handles output after completion.
features.background: Enrichment findings in SQLite. Embabel framework configured.
business_rules: ExtractionOrchestrator queries SQLite for ALL Phase 1 and enrichment data before agent invocation
CodebaseKnowledge contains StructuralGraph, SemanticEnrichment, and LinkRegistry sub-models
Query methods: getEntryPoints(), getCallersOf(), getCalleesOf(), getComponentsByType(), getAllKnownMethods(), findUnresolvedLinks()
getEntryPoints() returns all entry point types (HTTP, SCHEDULED, KAFKA, RABBITMQ, ACTIVEMQ, EVENT_LISTENER)

features.name: Embabel Agent — Entry-Point-Driven Extraction
features.description: The Embabel agent discovers entry points (HTTP, scheduled, Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, EventListener), traces execution flows through the call graph, extracts business semantics (user stories, Gherkin scenarios, business rules, edge cases), groups related flows into features using semantic clustering, resolves cross-flow dependencies, and produces Markdown + JSON output. Supports sub-chain caching, orphaned method detection, and progressive disclosure.
features.background: CodebaseKnowledge available. Embabel framework configured.
business_rules: Entry points are scored by priority (enrichment availability + complexity + user-facing + test file)
Trivial endpoints (actuator, health, metrics) are filtered out
Flow tracing uses sub-chain caching to avoid redundant service chain analysis
Adaptive depth: max-flow-depth (default: 8) caps call chain exploration
Progressive disclosure: MINIMAL/STANDARD/FULL output based on complexity score
Semantic clustering groups related flows into features using enrichment similarity where available
Orphaned methods unreachable from any entry point are flagged
Guardrails: max-flow-depth (8), max-tokens-per-run (500000)

features.name: Quality Audit — Schema Validation (Simplified)

business_rules: SemanticManifestWriter validates JSON output against PRD §6.2 schema before persisting
Schema validation failure sets Phase 3 marker to FAILED
Quarantined flows appear in spec Section 5 with review_required: true in manifest
Audit is pure Java — runs inside output writers, not as a separate step

features.name: Domain Model + Output Writers
features.description: Pure-Java domain classes for Phase 3 synthesis output (EntryPoint, ExecutionFlow, FlowStep, FunctionalFlow, GherkinScenario, BusinessRule, EdgeCase, ExternalCall, NonFunctionalRequirement, etc.) and writers that produce Markdown spec and semantic JSON manifest from the extraction cache.

features.name: Spring XML Configuration Analysis
features.description: DOM-based parsing of Spring XML configuration files to extract bean declarations, component scans, AOP config, JMS listeners, scheduled tasks, namespace beans, and alias definitions. Supports <import> recursion, @ImportResource Java annotation bridge, and classpath/file-style resource resolution with glob patterns.
features.background: Scan target directories discovered and .xml files filtered via XmlBeanAnalyzer.isSpringXmlConfig().
business_rules: Only Spring XML files (root namespace http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans) are analyzed — non-Spring XML is silently skipped
<bean> elements are parsed for id, class, scope, and factory-method; <alias> mappings capture name-to-target pairs
Elements in 13 known Spring namespaces are resolved to Java types via a namespace registry
Infrastructure config is flagged: <aop:config>, <tx:*>, <cache:*> as AOP/TX config; <context:component-scan> for base packages
Scheduled tasks from <task:scheduled> and JMS listeners from <jms:listener> are extracted with all attributes
<import> chains are followed recursively with cycle detection via a visited-set
classpath:/classpath*:/file: resource prefixes and glob patterns supported via ResourcePathResolver
@ImportResource on Java classes bridges to XML analysis, attributing XML findings to the Java file's result

user_stories.title: Developer discovers Spring XML bean declarations
Developer discovers scheduled tasks and JMS listeners from XML
Developer traces Spring XML configuration across imports

features.name: @Bean Method Detection (Java Configuration)
features.description: Detects @Bean-annotated methods in @Configuration and @SpringBootApplication classes, capturing explicit or implicit bean names, return types, declaring class, and source file path.
features.background: Java source files analyzed in Pass 2 by JavaAstAnalyzer.
business_rules: @Bean methods in @Configuration and @SpringBootApplication classes are detected
Explicit bean names from @Bean("name"), @Bean(name="name"), and @Bean(value="name") are extracted
First name from array form @Bean(name={"a","b"}) is used as the primary bean name
Implicit bean names fall back to the method name
Interfaces and abstract classes are skipped
Classes without @Configuration or @SpringBootApplication are skipped
